title: Minimize Disappointed Integers
statement:
You are given an array `arr` of `n` positive integers. In a given arrangement of the array, the integer at index `i` is **disappointed** if the sum of the integers at indices `0` to `i - 1` is **strictly greater** than the integer at index `i`. The first integer has an empty prefix (sum `0`), so it is never disappointed.

The **total disappointment** of an arrangement is the number of disappointed integers in it.

You may rearrange the integers in any order. Print the **minimum** total disappointment that can be achieved.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers `arr[0] ... arr[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum possible total disappointment.

examples.explanation: Arranged as `1 1 2 4` the prefix sums before each element are `0, 1, 2, 4`. Each element is at least its prefix sum, so nobody is disappointed.

Arrange as `1 1 5 10 1`: the prefix sums are `0, 1, 2, 7, 17`, and only the last `1` (17 > 1) is disappointed. No arrangement avoids it: among the three 1s, the third one always sees a prefix of at least 2.
The first 4 sees 0, the second sees 4 (not strictly greater), the third sees 8 > 4 and is disappointed.

hints: A disappointed integer still adds to the prefix sum of everything after it, so it is best to move disappointed integers to the very end.
That leaves a front part where nobody is disappointed. Which order lets the prefix sum grow as slowly as possible?
Sort ascending and scan with a running sum: keep an element if it is at least the current sum (add it to the sum), otherwise it is disappointed and is skipped.
